question: A forensic physician examining a person charged with murder finds that the accused has a known diagnosis of schizophrenia but behaved rationally for three days before the act. Which statement about the 'lucid interval' is CORRECT in this forensic context?

answers.text: A lucid interval means the underlying mental disorder is in remission and the diagnosis should be revised.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A lucid interval does not imply remission or diagnostic revision — the disorder persists; it is a period of temporary restoration of rational capacity within the course of the illness.

answers.text: Acts committed during a lucid interval may attract full criminal responsibility despite the underlying mental illness.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. If the accused had the capacity to understand the nature and wrongfulness of the act during a lucid interval, the McNaughten defence will not apply — full criminal responsibility may be established.

answers.text: The existence of a lucid interval automatically establishes fitness to plead in all legal proceedings.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Fitness to plead is assessed at the time of the trial, not retrospectively. A lucid interval at the time of the act addresses criminal responsibility, not fitness to stand trial.

answers.text: ICD-11 requires a minimum duration of 72 hours for a period to qualify as a lucid interval.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ICD-11 does not specify a minimum duration for a lucid interval; its forensic significance depends on the quality of rational capacity restored, not on a fixed time threshold.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the 'Lucid Interval' content section. The key principle: a mental illness diagnosis does not automatically preclude criminal responsibility — the physician must document whether a lucid interval existed at the time of the act.
Well done. The lucid interval is central to forensic psychiatric assessment: rational capacity during the act can negate the insanity defence regardless of an established diagnosis.
